name: Japanese Proverbs
summary: Timeless Japanese aphorisms and kotowaza embodying resilience, mindfulness, nature, and the beauty of impermanence.
bio: Japanese proverbs (kotowaza) represent centuries of contemplative insight shaped by Zen Buddhism, Shinto reverence for nature, and the lived realities of feudal resilience. Often expressed in concise four-character idioms (yojijukugo) or poetic sayings, they distill profound psychological and ethical truths. Rather than abstract metaphysics, Japanese folk wisdom focuses on practical demeanor: how one meets misfortune, how one honors transience, and how small daily disciplines compound into mastery.

keyWorks.title: Hojoki (Kamo no Chomei)

keyWorks.title: Tsurezuregusa (Yoshida Kenko)

keyWorks.title: Hagakure & Bushido Precepts
keyWorks.description: Maxims on resolute duty, sincerity, and presence in the face of mortality.

pillars.concept: Nana Korobi Ya Oki (七転び八起き)
pillars.description: Fall down seven times, stand up eight — the sovereign virtue of unyielding resilience.
One time, one meeting — treasuring each encounter as an unrepeatable gift of presence.
Finding profound beauty in simplicity, modesty, asymmetry, and weathered impermanence.
A gentle, poignant empathy for the ephemeral nature of all living things.

whyTimeless: Japanese proverbs provide a poetic sanctuary against modern hurry, teaching us to embrace imperfection, cultivate quiet fortitude, and honor the sacred in ordinary moments.
